newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major argues for EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major argues for EMU delay.

text.p: Former British prime minister John Major said on Tuesday he would argue for a delay in the European single currency if he was still in power.

Major said the change of government in France and the debate about the German government's desire to revalue its gold made it unlikely the currency could go ahead on time on January 1, 1999. "It seems to me almost possible to dismiss any chance of the right economic conditions being there," he said.

Major, who during the election campaign maintained a policy of taking part in negotiations and only deciding later whether or not to join the single currency, said in a BBC interview that he had changed his mind because events had changed.

"Events have changed in France and events have changed in Germany. We have to respond to those changing events...What I have said is; as a result of those events we must now say it's not safe to go ahead on the 1st of January 1999," Major said.

Major, who is standing aside as Conservative leader after Labour's crushing victory, said the new Prime Minister Tony Blair should use Britain's "voice and...vote" at the European Union summit in Amsterdam later this month to make this clear. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
